about: The structure of a Broadcast plugin repo. `broadcast-plugin check` and the plugin store read these same rules, so a repo that passes the check here passes the store's structure check. Paths are relative to the repo root and use /. A folder path ends with /. An error stops a submission; a warning does not. The matching rules are in `matching`; plugin-repo-vectors.json has shared cases that both checks must pass.

matching.result: Each problem is {id, level, path?}. Rule problems have no path; forbidden, symlink and dist problems name the path (a folder path ends with /). Compare results as a set.
matching.file: kind file: that path is a regular file that is not forbidden.
matching.anyFile: kind anyFile: at least one of paths is a regular file.
matching.folder: kind folder: that folder holds at least one regular file at any depth that is not forbidden (a test/.env alone does not count).
matching.absent: kind absent: a problem when that path exists (file or folder); the problem has the path.
matching.forbidden: pattern matches the NAME of a file or folder at any depth, case-insensitive. * matches zero or more characters and never /. A name in forbiddenExceptions is never forbidden. A forbidden folder is reported once with its path and is not looked into.
matching.skip: skip names are skipped at the repo root only, with everything in them.
matching.symlinks: a symbolic link anywhere is an error (id symlink, with its path) and is not followed.
matching.limits: limits count regular files that are not skipped, not forbidden and not inside a forbidden folder. maxBytes is the sum of their sizes. Over a limit: a problem with the limit's id.
matching.manifest: manifest.json present but not valid JSON or not an object: error id manifest-json, and manifest.required is not checked. A required dotted key is missing when absent, null, or a string that is empty after trim; a key under a part that is not an object (for example requires: false or 0) is absent. Error id manifest.<key>. manifest.json absent: only the rule manifest.
matching.hardLinks: a hard link in a file tree is a regular file. (The store refuses hard-link and other special entries in a fetched archive; that is outside this spec.)

rules.message: manifest.json is missing. It names the plugin, its version, the Broadcast versions it supports and its permissions.
The plugin code is missing: add src/main.ts or src/main.js.
README.md is missing. The store shows it on the plugin page.
AGENTS.md is missing. It tells coding agents how to build this plugin; copy it from the template.
test/ is missing or empty. Add at least one test (see the template).
CLAUDE.md is missing. The template's CLAUDE.md points Claude Code to AGENTS.md.
kit/ is missing. A pinned copy of the plugin kit lets CI build and test with no Broadcast server.
.github/workflows/ is missing. The template's workflow runs build, test and check on each push.
.gitignore is missing. It keeps dist/, packages and secrets out of the repo.
dist/ is built by `broadcast-plugin build` and by the plugin store. Remove it from the repo and add it to .gitignore.

imports.about: Before a build, every module in src/ may import only other files in src/. Checked: src/ files with a sourceExtension. Patterns: import "x", import ... from "x", export ... from "x", import("x"), require("x"); any `from` followed by a string counts. Strings, template literals, comments and regular expression literals are told apart by a tokenizer; a name after . (obj.import) is not a pattern. import()/require() must take one plain string (a template without ${} counts as plain). A specifier must start with ./ or ../, may not hold a backslash, and resolved (query and hash removed) must stay in src/. Each problem is {id, level, path, specifier?, call?}: call is import() or require() for import-computed. The same problem in one file is reported once.

import-backslash.message: %{path} imports "%{specifier}": a path with a backslash is not allowed. Use /.

import-not-relative.message: %{path} imports "%{specifier}": only files in src/ can be imported, with ./ or ../. The store builds with no npm, jsr or node packages and no network; copy the code into src/.

import-outside-src.message: %{path} imports "%{specifier}": the path leaves src/. Only files in src/ can be imported.

import-css.message: %{path} imports "%{specifier}": CSS is not bundled into dist/main.js. Put styles in ui/.

import-computed.message: %{path}: %{call} must take one plain string such as './file.js'. The store does not bundle computed paths.

build.about: How dist/main.js is built, by `broadcast-plugin build` and by the plugin store from a repo: esbuild <entry> <flags> --outfile=dist/main.js, with only src/ present. The store pins this esbuild version; the kit warns when the local one differs. Imports must be relative (./ or ../) and stay inside src/.
